evals.name: poster-row-focus-navigation
evals.prompt: I'm building a TV home screen with @lightningjs/core (Lightning v2). I have a `PosterRow` component that renders a horizontal row of movie poster tiles from an array of movie objects (title, image). Right now the remote control does nothing on this row — left/right don't move between posters and Enter doesn't do anything. Add focus handling so the user can navigate between posters with left/right and pressing Enter logs the selected movie's title to the console. Here's my component.
evals.expected_output: An updated PosterRow component that implements _getFocused() returning the currently selected poster child, an _handleRight()/_handleLeft() pair (or equivalent) that moves an index and re-requests focus, and an _handleEnter() (typically on the focused child or delegated) that logs the selected movie's title. Should use Lightning's real focus/key-handling conventions, not invented DOM event listeners.
assertions: The component implements _getFocused() returning the currently focused poster child (Lightning's real focus delegation mechanism)
Left/right navigation is implemented via Lightning key-handler methods (e.g. _handleLeft/_handleRight) that update a tracked selected index, not via DOM event listeners
Pressing Enter logs the selected movie's title to the console (via _handleEnter on the row or its child, or an equivalent delegation)
No DOM/CSS/React syntax is introduced (no addEventListener, document, className, style={{}}, JSX)
The selected index is bounds-checked so navigating past the first/last poster doesn't throw or select an out-of-range item

evals.name: button-js-to-ts-template-spec
evals.prompt: Can you convert this Lightning v2 JavaScript Button component to TypeScript? I want real typing on the template refs and props, not just slapping `any` everywhere — the `label` setter and `onEnter` callback prop should be properly typed too. Here's the file.
evals.expected_output: A .ts version of Button that defines a proper TemplateSpec (extends Lightning.Component.TemplateSpec) with PascalCase children (Background, Label) and camelCase properties (onEnter, label), implements TypeConfig/typed refs so this.tag('Label')/getByRef('Label') is typed, and types the onEnter callback as a function type rather than any.
assertions: Defines a TypeScript TemplateSpec type/interface (e.g. extends Lightning.Component.TemplateSpec) rather than typing the whole class as any
Template child refs (Background, Label) use PascalCase and are distinguished from camelCase properties (onEnter, label) per Lightning's TS conventions
The onEnter callback prop has a real function type (e.g. () => void), not any
Uses getByRef() (or another typed accessor) rather than untyped tag() calls for accessing typed children
The resulting file is valid TypeScript syntax (.ts extension, class property type annotations, no leftover untyped any on the public props)

evals.name: modal-signal-handler-bug
evals.prompt: My Lightning v2 Modal component is supposed to notify its parent when it closes so the parent can hide it and update its own state, but the parent's handler never seems to fire. Here are the modal component and the relevant parent code — what's wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that `this.signal('modalClosed')` is silently dropped because Lightning requires the parent to opt in with a `signals` map declared at the template site where the child is instantiated (`Modal: { type: Modal, signals: { modalClosed: '_handleModalClosed' } }`) — the Parent template has no such map at all. Fixes it by adding that `signals` map. Also ideally notices that the existing `$modalClosed()` method inside the `Modal` state is separate dead code: `$`-prefixed names are the `fireAncestors()` convention, and Modal never calls `fireAncestors`, so renaming things without adding the `signals` map would not fix the bug.
assertions: Identifies that this.signal() requires the parent to declare a signals (or passSignals) map at the template site where the child is instantiated, and that the Modal entry in Parent's template has no such map
Provides a concrete fix that adds a signals map (e.g. signals: { modalClosed: '_handleModalClosed' }) to the Modal template entry in Parent

Recognizes that the $modalClosed() method inside the Modal state is unrelated dead code because $-prefixed names are the fireAncestors() convention, not the signal() convention, and Modal never calls fireAncestors
Does not claim the bug is purely a _handleModalClosed vs $modalClosed naming mismatch without also identifying the missing signals map, since renaming alone would not fix the bug
Does not misattribute the bug to something unrelated to Lightning's signal-wiring contract, like a DOM-style addEventListener pattern or a focus-delegation issue, as the primary cause
